coverage: since this morning (~08:00 Berlin) / last ~12 hours — afternoon edition skipped
headline: Witkoff and Kushner land in Moscow as Putin pauses Kyiv strikes; German police publish wanted photos in the power-grid sabotage manhunt; Dutch central bank shifts gold out of the US and Canada.

stories.title: Witkoff & Kushner in Moscow; Putin orders a Kyiv strike pause
facts: CNN: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Moscow Sat with a Trump “proposal to end the war”; Kyiv visit planned for Sunday
Kremlin: Putin ordered a three-day halt to strikes on Kyiv from midnight Sat local — capital only, not the rest of Ukraine — tied to the US contacts
Zelenskyy: Ukraine ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow through Monday if Russia matches on Kyiv; says he spoke with the envoys Sat
Earlier Sat Zelenskyy said Russian missiles hit airports near Kyiv (incl. Boryspil) amid talk of a US aircraft arrival
Peskov downplayed “new ideas”; Russian officials still insist any deal must reflect “realities on the ground”
stories.whyItMatters: First Kyiv trip for Trump’s envoys this term, paired with a narrow capital-only strike pause — a live diplomacy window, not a ceasefire.

image.alt: Kirill Dmitriev welcomes Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff in Moscow

stories.title: Wanted photos out: manhunt for grid-sabotage suspect Daniel V.
facts: ZEIT/dpa Sat: police + prosecutors publish a wanted notice with two photos of the 48-year-old from Gevelsberg; public tips sought
Suspect still missing after SEK stormed his flat (explosives found) and a converted truck at Hambacher Forst — he wasn’t in either
Bekennerschreiben claim attacks near brown-coal sites in NRW + Brandenburg; Dobrindt calls it likely “Klimaterrorismus” / Einzeltäter
Sachsen: police secured multiple Sprengvorrichtungen near Umspannwerke (Bärwalde / Graustein area); link to other cases under review
Amprion CEO: public grid maps make attacks too easy — wants looser transparency rules + broader drone/camera surveillance rights
stories.whyItMatters: A live critical-infra manhunt with published faces, plus a policy fight over how much grid detail stays online.

image.alt: Converted truck linked to the German power-grid sabotage suspect

stories.title: Netherlands shifts dozens of tonnes of gold out of the US and Canada
facts: ABC: De Nederlandsche Bank moved 86 tonnes of gold held in the US/Canada (of 313 there) to the Bank of England between March and August
DNB cites “crisis preparedness” and “increasing geopolitical unrest”; gold at BoE is “most easily tradable” in a crunch
Mix of physical shipments to Zeist then UK, plus sell-in-NY / buy-in-London for 59 tonnes to cut relocation risk
Netherlands total reserves ~612 tonnes; France also replaced New York holdings with Europe-stored gold in 2025
HN #1 Sat (~296 pts / 190 comments) — feed is reading it as a trust-in-US story
stories.whyItMatters: A quiet central-bank logistics story that the tech feed is treating as a geopolitical signal.

stories.title: Bay Area tech cuts already past all of 2025 — AI as the stated reason
facts: heise (Mercury News WARN data): Bay Area firms have filed ~12,947 tech layoffs YTD through early Sep — ~27% above the full-year 2025 total (10,170)
Meta leads the Bay Area tally (~3,715 local of a ~10% global cut framed as funding AI spend); Amazon 917, Cisco 706, Oracle 652 in the Valley counts
TrueUp via Yahoo: >180k global tech layoffs logged for 2026 after >245k in 2025; trackers attribute >92k cuts explicitly to AI
Oracle’s annual report: ~21k roles cut worldwide (~13%) with AI scaling cited; Block ~40% workforce cut also in the heise roundup
stories.whyItMatters: The layoff wave is no longer a 2023 hangover story — firms are openly trading headcount for AI capex mid-year.

image.alt: Illustration for heise coverage of tech-sector job cuts

stories.title: Astra tops DeepsecBench on X as OpenAI’s Critical cyber model lands
facts: OpenAI (3–4 Sep): GPT-6 Astra is first model at Critical cyber capability under the Preparedness Framework — autonomous vuln discovery/exploit potential
The Hacker News: Astra scores 100% on ExploitBench (vs ~78.5% for GPT-5.6 Sol); public build refuses PoC exploit requests, focuses on review/patching
Vercel / @rauchg Sat: Astra leads DeepsecBench — ~49 min vs ~4h for Sol on their cited run, similar cost, claimed better score
Advanced offensive cyber access stays gated (Daybreak); Saturday Following feed is mostly benchmark + harness chatter
stories.whyItMatters: Morning skipped the Astra drop; Saturday’s feed is the first big Following-wave on the cyber-capability framing.
